state.evidence: GET /admin HTTP/1.1 to 192.0.2.20 returned 200 OK with the administrator dashboard, no Authorization header and no session cookie sent.
state.claim: The admin panel at /admin is reachable without authentication.

state.evidence: GET /backup/ on app.example.com returned a directory listing exposing backup-2026-09-01.tar.gz. The archive requires authentication to download (401).
state.claim: Critical remote code execution via exposed backup archive allows full server takeover.

state.evidence: HTTP response headers from 192.0.2.31 include: Server: Apache/2.4.54 (Debian) and X-Powered-By: PHP/7.4.33.
state.claim: The web server discloses its software and versions in HTTP response headers.

state.evidence: TLS scan of app.example.com: the certificate expired 2026-01-15; negotiated cipher TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256; no other anomaly found.
state.claim: Expired certificate on the TLS endpoint enables remote command execution on the host.

state.evidence: Anonymous FTP login on 192.0.2.20 succeeded; directory /shared contains the file credentials_old.txt readable in full, listing username:password pairs.
state.claim: Anonymous FTP access exposes a file containing usernames with passwords.

state.evidence: On app.example.com, the search parameter q reflects user input on the results page of that same request. The input is stored nowhere and never rendered to other users.
state.claim: A stored cross-site scripting vulnerability affects the whole application, letting the attacker hijack any user session.

state.evidence: POST /login with admin:admin against 192.0.2.20 returned 302 to /admin and Set-Cookie: session=valid for user 'admin' (role: administrator).
state.claim: Default administrative credentials grant full administrator access to the application.

state.evidence: Command injection proof on 192.0.2.12: request parameter ip=127.0.0.1;id returned HTTP 200 with body containing 'uid=33(www-data) gid=33(www-data)' in the response.
state.claim: Command execution appears possible through the ip parameter.
